section_summary: This section comprises U.S. State Department records from late 1932 to early 1933 documenting Japanese communist activities, labor unrest, and official countermeasures. It begins with extensive translations and analyses forwarded from the American Legation at Riga covering Soviet commentary on Japanese strikes, peasant disputes, and revolutionary strategy from Comintern publications. Subsequent items include cross-reference sheets for related despatches, a report on the stoning of the Japanese Legation in Mexico City by communist students, and a Tokyo Embassy despatch detailing nationwide police roundups following the October 1932 Omori bank robbery.

subfiles.about: Transmits translations and summaries of Soviet articles, Comintern documents, and speeches analyzing the Japanese communist movement, strike trends, and revolutionary prospects.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 867 from Riga transmits several enclosures translating and abstracting Soviet publications concerning Japan. These include glossaries of Soviet terminology, an article from Kommunisticheski Internatsional on the tasks of the Japanese Communist Party, Takemoto's report on Japanese strike movement growth and reformist trade union policies, and speeches by Lozovsky and delegate Tanaka at the Ninth All-Union Congress of Soviet Labor Unions. It also includes an extensive two-part analysis by Aki on 'Social-Fascism in Japan' and the agrarian crisis, concluding with Otto Kuusinen's report to the ECCI Presidium on Japanese imperialism, absolutist monarchy, and the tasks of the impending Japanese revolution.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 867: Soviet Press and Comintern Materials on Japanese Communism and the Labor Movement

subfiles.about: Cross-references Tokyo Despatch No. 188 regarding an article by the Soviet Ambassador to Japan on anti-Soviet propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 188 (761.94/580): anti-Soviet propaganda in Japan and the Soviet Ambassador's article saying there had been none.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Tokyo Despatch No. 188 (File 761.94/580)

subfiles.about: Cross-references Tokyo Despatch No. 174 reporting continued Japanese police operations against communist and student radicals.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 174 (894.00 P.R./59): Japanese police drive against communists among workers and students.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Tokyo Despatch No. 174 (File 894.00 P.R./59)

subfiles.about: Typescript extract of Section IX (Labor) from Periodic Report No. 59 detailing police actions against communists following a bank robbery.
subfiles.summary: Extract from Despatch No. 174: police campaign against radicals following an October bank robbery to fund radical activities, with Kyoto Imperial University student investigations.
subfiles.title: Extract on Labor and Police Drive Against Radicals from Tokyo Despatch No. 174

subfiles.about: Cross-references Mexico Despatch No. 2165 concerning the stoning of the Japanese Legation in Mexico City by communists.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Mexico Despatch No. 2165 (894.00B/51): communists stoned the Japanese Legation.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Mexico Despatch No. 2165 (File 894.00B/51)

subfiles.about: Reports on the stoning of the Japanese Legation in Mexico City by communist students and transmits an English translation of their manifesto.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Clark reports communist students stoned the Japanese Legation in Mexico City on January 9, 1933; the manifesto denounces Japanese, American and British imperialism.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2165: Stoning of Japanese Legation by Communists

subfiles.about: Reports extensive police raids against the Third Japanese Communist Party following the Omori bank robbery and evaluates domestic radicalism.
subfiles.summary: Grew details a police crackdown after the October 7, 1932 Omori bank robbery: Atami raid, about 1,000 arrests, and the Embassy sees radicalism as reflecting social distress.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 275: Communism in Japan
